issues.legal_issue: A building-plan application for residential use cannot be rejected on the basis of a proposed development plan that has not been brought into force.
material_facts: The owners’ land had been permitted for non-agricultural use and was being used for residential purposes within a residential area.
A building-plan application was filed while the existing comprehensive development plan remained in force.
The planning authority rejected the application because the land fell within a valley zone identified in a proposed revised plan.
The proposed revised plan had not been approved or brought into force; the State was still considering objections to it.
issues.conclusion: The proposed revised plan could not provide a lawful basis for rejecting the application. The rejection and the Division Bench judgment upholding it were set aside, and the authority was directed to consider the application under the law in force.
issues.legal_principle: The right to property includes the right to construct, although legislation may regulate that right. A restriction on construction must have a clear basis in law; an anticipated or proposed change cannot take away the right before it becomes effective. Ecological considerations do not permit a court or authority to substitute a proposed planning rule for the law in force. The Court relied on the principles in Director of Public Works v. Ho Po Sang, Howrah Municipal Corporation v. Ganges Rope Co. Ltd., and Kuldeep Singh v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi; it also noted that planning legislation governs ecological aspects.

rule.if: building_plan_appeal and residential_use_permitted and existing_plan_in_force and proposed_revision_unapproved and rejection_based_on_proposed_revision

predicates.building_plan_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the rejection of an application for approval of building plans.
predicates.residential_use_permitted: The landowners were permitted to use the land for non-agricultural residential purposes.
predicates.existing_plan_in_force: An existing development plan remained legally in force when the application was considered.
predicates.proposed_revision_unapproved: A proposed revised development plan had not been approved or brought into force.
predicates.rejection_based_on_proposed_revision: The planning authority rejected the application because of a restriction identified in the proposed revision.

issues.definition: When a building-plan appeal concerns residential land governed by an existing plan and the rejection rests on an unapproved revision, the proposed revision cannot supply the legal basis for that rejection.

issues.legal_issue: A building-plan application must be decided under the law applicable when permission is granted, including any statutory change that has become effective by then.
material_facts: The application for building-plan approval remained pending while a revised development plan was under consideration.
The proposed revision had not been brought into force when the authority rejected the application.
The Court stated that building-plan applications are to be decided according to the law applicable on the day permission is granted.
issues.conclusion: The application had to be considered under the law in force when permission was to be granted, not under a proposed plan that had not become effective.
issues.legal_principle: An application does not confer a vested right to obtain approval under the rules in force when it was filed. In Howrah Municipal Corporation v. Ganges Rope Co. Ltd., the Court held that a settled expectation cannot prevail over statutory rules that are amended during the pendency of an application. Director of Public Works v. Ho Po Sang was cited on the distinction between a mere expectation and an acquired right. The Court stated that the law applicable on the date permission is granted governs the application, and relied on Kuldeep Singh v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi concerning the authority’s duty to exercise its jurisdiction within a reasonable time.

predicates.building_plan_application_pending: An application for approval of building plans remained undecided.
predicates.planning_law_changes_before_decision: The governing planning law changed after the application was filed but before it was decided.
predicates.new_rule_effective_when_permission_is_co: The new rule had become legally effective by the time permission was considered.

issues.definition: If a building-plan application is pending when planning law changes and the new rule is effective by the time permission is considered, the application is decided under that effective rule.

issues.legal_issue: A planning authority must decide a building-plan application within a reasonable time.
material_facts: The owners filed an application for approval of building plans and responded to queries raised by the authority.
The application remained unresolved, and the owners asserted that the delay entitled them to proceed with construction.
The Court directed the authority to consider the application promptly and within a specified period.
issues.conclusion: The planning authority was required to exercise its jurisdiction within a reasonable time and was directed to consider the application within eight weeks.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory authority must exercise its jurisdiction within a reasonable time. The Court relied on Kuldeep Singh v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi for that principle and directed consideration of the application under the applicable law.

predicates.building_plan_application_pending: An application for approval of building plans remains undecided.
predicates.planning_authority_has_duty_to_decide: The planning authority is responsible for considering and deciding the application.

issues.definition: When a building-plan application remains pending before an authority responsible for deciding it, the authority must decide it within a reasonable time.
